instruction: Save a screenshot of the video's present frame to the Desktop as 'frame_capture.png', making sure the image is a minimum of 640 pixels wide.

parameters.window_name: Interstellar Movie - Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer - VLC media player

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires taking a video screenshot with specific minimum dimensions (640x360 pixels). Evaluator checks: (1) file exists at Desktop location, (2) file is valid PNG format, (3) image dimensions meet minimum requirements (width >= 640px, height >= 360px). This variation tests ability to verify image properties beyond just file existence.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: file location (/home/user/Desktop/frame_capture.png), PNG format, and minimum width (640 pixels)
Getter logic correctly extracts image state using PIL: file existence, dimensions (width/height), and format validation
Metric logic correctly compares dimensions against minimum requirements with appropriate scoring breakdown (30% existence, 20% format, 50% dimensions)
Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts right state -> metric compares right aspects -> expected values match instruction requirements
Edge cases handled properly: returns 0.0 if file doesn't exist, handles image reading errors gracefully, uses temporary file for safety
Practical feasibility verified: getter can access Desktop files via env.controller.get_file(), PIL can read PNG and extract dimensions, no postconfig needed
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Expected rules include min_height=360 which is not explicitly mentioned in instruction (instruction only specifies 'at least 640 pixels wide'). This is an additional quality constraint that doesn't prevent verification but goes slightly beyond stated requirements.
